studies.title: Physical objects and HUD information
studies.sourceBasis: Primary design literature, existing Oracle studies, user screenshot and static coffee source inspection. No usability test or corrected live game claimed.
studies.assetNote: No game-package extraction is claimed by this design lesson.

claims.title: Separate the physical object from player information
claims.finding: The asset represents the object itself: cup, handle, saucer, machine casing, buttons, spout and tray. Next-action prompts, selection, recipe progress and teaching hints belong to a separate presentation layer addressed to the player. The HUD is a conduit for information beyond what the player can infer by seeing and hearing the world. This is Evan’s project requirement, recorded 2026-10-21.
claims.basis: explicit project requirement; not a claim about all games

claims.title: Beyond the HUD — Fagerholt & Lorentzon (2009), sections 7.1–7.2 and 10.1.1
claims.finding: The thesis separates whether information belongs to the fiction from where it is drawn. A spatial cue can sit in 3D without being an object in the fiction; conventional HUD information is presented as an overlay. Its research concerns FPS immersion, so application to this coffee game is a design inference.
claims.basis: primary design literature; bounded reading, not full-book study

evidence.path: Beyond the HUD — Fagerholt & Lorentzon (2009), sections 7.1–7.2 and 10.1.1

claims.title: Signifiers, not affordances — Don Norman (2008)
claims.finding: Norman distinguishes possible actions from perceivable clues that help people understand them. Our application: an interaction cue must communicate what the player can do without implying a misleading physical feature.
claims.basis: primary design literature; bounded reading, not full-book study

claims.title: Coffee counterexample: a prompt became a yellow solid
claims.finding: The supplied screenshot shows a thick yellow ring around the cup that reads as another physical component. Inspected coffee-station source creates a lit TorusGeometry, follows the current action target and pulses its scale. It is a runtime guidance mesh, not evidence that a downloaded asset contains the ring. The error is the visual and architectural mixing of guidance with the world object.
claims.basis: user screenshot and static coffee-station source inspection; corrected runtime not verified

claims.title: Asset, world feedback and interface are distinct responsibilities
claims.finding: Author and export clean physical assets. Keep interaction anchors and target IDs as metadata. World feedback may include coffee flowing, steam, liquid level or a plausible machine indicator, driven by actual state. Keep selection, step hints and progress in a separately removable interface layer; these must not alter asset geometry, collision, physical bounds or exported models. A deliberately world-anchored cue remains interface and must read that way.
claims.basis: original implementation guidance; proposed, not shipped

claims.title: Coffee correction and review criteria
claims.finding: Remove the yellow guidance torus. Use a concise next-action label and progress in the right drawer, with optional narration and an equivalent visible cue when muted. If a target needs locating, use restrained screen-space focus treatment tied to its stable ID, clearly distinct from material. Preserve left navigation. Review every recipe step at desktop and phone size with guidance on/off, narration muted, and drawers closed; keep the cup silhouette intact and ensure the next valid action remains discoverable.
claims.basis: project-specific design inference; correction remains unimplemented in this research update

claims.title: Manufactured construction: inset gauges, fitted parts
claims.finding: Evan rejects the clay-like espresso machine. Build the fascia around a gauge recess: dial face behind glass, thin bezel at the opening, a shallow shadow gap, and a body seated into the casing. Knobs project from defined shafts or mounts; they are not gauge faces. Use controlled edge radii, panel thickness, seams and material differences between painted metal, stainless steel, glass and ceramic. Friendly stylization must preserve these assembly relationships.
claims.basis: Evan’s art direction and original construction proposal; geometry not yet corrected

claims.title: Use manufacturer references to establish what each part does
claims.finding: La Marzocco’s Linea Mini manual identifies separate brew-group and steam-boiler pressure gauges. This supports modeling gauges as functional instruments. Inset depth, glass, bezel proportions and panel construction are this project’s proposed treatment, not dimensions recovered from the manual. Do not imply accurate pressure simulation from an animated needle.
claims.basis: manufacturer documentation; functional reference, not engineering reconstruction

evidence.path: Linea Mini operating manual, gauge identification

lesson.text: A 3D asset is the object itself. Treat player guidance as an explicit, independent information channel. Ask of every visible element: does it physically exist in the fiction, or is it communicating to the player? Choose presentation deliberately. Do not make a HUD cue look like an unexplained object part.
lesson.status: Project requirement plus design inference; coffee correction not implemented or verified.

studies.nextPass: Apply the correction to the coffee game and verify each step through live MCP plus desktop/mobile rendering. Existing Oracle Black & White and Mindustry studies inform interaction and HUD state but do not prove this design works for players. Reconstruct the machine fascia with inset instruments and inspect front and oblique views; check gauge recess, glass, thin bezel, knob mounts and distinct materials.
